name: testland/test-removal-criteria
description: Decides which existing tests should stop existing, using five removal classes (duplicate, tautology, trivial, dead-signal, orphan) and a four-condition delete gate where every condition must hold or the verdict reverts to keep. Puts the burden of proof on removal: each deletion carries a written reason, redundant-coverage evidence from a per-test source map, and a named reviewer; a test that has merely never failed is treated as possibly load-bearing, not worthless. Use when a suite has outgrown its signal value and someone is opening a pruning change set that deletes test files; for choosing which tests to RUN per change (not delete) use regression-suite-selector, and to track accumulating low-value coverage over time use the coverage debt ledger in qa-test-reporting's test-coverage-targeter.
